subject: WaveHealth: fit confirmation & integration runbook
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@wavehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: WaveHealth — quick follow-up and recommended runbook

Alyssa — thanks again for the conversation earlier. I wanted to capture the pains, goals, and a recommended path we discussed so we have a single source of truth going into the technical deep-dive.

High-level call takeaways
- Pain: triage latency in patient intake (avg 1.2s per call today) and noisy candidate lists when surfacing next-best actions for clinicians.
- Compliance: data is PHI; WaveHealth is leaning towards a VPC/private deployment for initial rollout.
- Product goals: 90th percentile latency < 500ms for inline triage, ability to stream partial results to the clinician UI, structured JSON outputs that map to FHIR-ish fields, and reranking of candidate suggestions using embeddings.

Proposed integration approach
1) API & runtime: start with a private Redwood deployment in their AWS VPC (we discussed Dedicated vs Private — they prefer Private with customer-managed VPC).
2) Streaming & function-calling: use streaming responses for the triage flow so the UI can show partial confidence scores; function-call hooks will invoke domain-specific enrichment (e.g., patient-history lookup) — we propose function schema v1 attached.
3) Structured outputs: return a compact JSON envelope (fields: intent, confidence, slots[], suggested_actions[]) that maps to their EHR adapter. We'll include a mapping guide in the runbook.
4) Embeddings & rerank: store candidate vectors in their vector DB and call our reranker endpoint for final ordering. We'll benchmark top-k (k=10) latency implications.

Immediate next steps (owners & due dates)
- Kimberly: draft SDK change list (streaming client + funcall helpers + structured output serializers) — due Tue 2027-04-06.
- Ben: pricing delta and committed-capacity estimate for Private deployment + rough unit economics — due Wed 2027-04-07.
- Sergio (me): schedule technical deep-dive with WaveHealth eng for week of Apr 11; share runbook draft now.

Attachments: integration-runbook-draft.pdf (overview + mapping), sdk-impact-matrix.xlsx (columns: sdk_component, effort, risk, compatibility).

Alyssa — would you confirm the right WaveHealth eng leads to invite (we had Matt and Priya on the call)? If a private deployment is confirmed we'll include our security checklist and KMS/HSM integration options.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@wavehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WaveHealth — quick follow-up and recommended runbook

Thanks, Sergio — this is helpful and captures things cleanly.

Confirmations / clarifications:
- Yes, please invite Matt Gomez (matt.g@wavehealth.com) and Priya Rao (priya.rao@wavehealth.com) to the deep-dive. Matt owns infra/hosting and Priya owns the EHR adapters.
- We are scoped to keep PHI in our VPC initially. Would like a brief security Q&A in the deep-dive (SOC2 scope, KMS, audit logs).
- On reranking: can you include expected P50/P95 latency for top-10 rerank calls in the SDK matrix? That will help our PE team evaluate.

Possible deep-dive windows: Apr 12 (after 11am PT) or Apr 13 (morning PT).

A couple of asks before the call:
- A short spec for the function-call schema you mentioned — even a markdown sketch will do.
- Any examples of the structured JSON envelope mapping to FHIR-ish fields.

Appreciate it — Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Product Lead, Clinical Automation | WaveHealth
alyssa@wavehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@wavehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WaveHealth — quick follow-up and recommended runbook

Looping in a couple of quick operational notes based on Alyssa's asks:
- Pricing: I'll produce two options — (A) Private deployment with a small committed GPU pool + usage overage; (B) Dedicated-reserved + canary burst to hosted for daytime spikes. We should show 3-month and 12-month cost lines.
- Benchmarks: Kimberly, can you add expected P50/P95 numbers for rerank top-10 and for streaming partial-result latency into the sdk-impact-matrix.xlsx? If we don't have exact numbers from a WaveHealth-like workload, add ranges and test plan notes.
- Security QA: I'll prep our SOC2 summary + KMS integration checklist for the deep-dive; Sergio, I'll send these as separate attachments before the call.

Also want to call out rollout strategy (for Alyssa): start with a single clinical workflow (intake triage), run a 4-week pilot with feature flags and traffic mirroring, then a phased rollout into prod. We'll attach a rollback playbook.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@wavehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WaveHealth — quick follow-up and recommended runbook

Kimberly — can you take the owner slot on the SDK change list and the initial function-call schema? Notes for the deliverable:
- SDK changes: streaming client example (JS/Python), funcall helpers (schema validation + convenient wrappers), structured output serializer with an example mapping to FHIR fields, and a small retry/backpressure guide for the client.
- Function schema sketch: include fields for call_id, patient_id (pseudonymized in our logs), timestamps, input_tokens, partial_confidence_scores, and an actions[] array (each action includes type, params, and estimated confidence).
- Performance notes: provide expected P50/P95 for the demo environment (we can use Redwood verified model profiles — reference the runbook) and a short test harness (curl + node script) so WaveHealth engineers can reproduce locally.

Kimberly, if you can share an initial SDK impact matrix by Apr 6 I will lock the deep-dive for Apr 12 11:30am PT and send calendar invites to Matt and Priya.

Thanks,
Sergio
